newsitem.title: USA: Union says will not strike at Unocal before Monday.
newsitem.headline: Union says will not strike at Unocal before Monday.

text.p: The union representing 900 workers at Unocal Corp's California refineries will not consider a strike before late Monday, a union official said Friday.

The Oil, Chemical, and Atomic Workers Union (OCAW) has threatened to terminate its contract with Unocal because of disagreement over the company's severance package. Termination leaves workers the option to strike.
"We wouldn't necessarily take any action before the early part of next week," said union representative Steve Sullivan. "Our position is...it would be Monday night," he said.
The union, which late Wednesday rejected a Unocal severance package, said it would offer an "orderly shutdown of the plant," if necessary.
No talks between Unocal and the union are scheduled for the weekend, Sullivan said.
Unocal's four refineries produce about 20 percent of California's gasoline, selling over 100,000 barrels per day (bpd).

The latest strike threat comes on the heels of the union's rejection last week of a labor contract from Tosco Corp, which plans to complete the purchase of the same Unocal refineries at the end of this month.
